item.title: Blanket ban on pets in social housing set to be reviewed
item.description: A working group is being set to review the blanket ban on pets in social housing. A commitment to review the code of practice applied by local authorities and approved housing bodies was included in the government's new housing plan launched last October. Fine Gael TD for Dublin Rathdown, Maeve O'Connell raised the matter in the Dáil this week. She says the Housing Minister confirmed he wants the ban on pets repealed as soon as possible: Advertisement

item.title: Gardaí respond to three-vehicle collision in Kiltoom
item.description: Gardaí and emergency services responded to a collision in Kiltoom, Co. Roscommon. The incident involved a tractor and two cars on the N61 shortly before 8pm yesterday evening. No injuries have been reported and no road closures are in place. One of the drivers, a woman in her 80s, was taken to hospital for assessment only. Advertisement

item.title: Over €870,000 in housing rents and annuities not paid to Roscommon County Council last year
item.description: Over 870,000 euro worth of housing rents and annuities were not paid to Roscommon County Council last year. Over 23,000 euro worth of housing loans also weren't repaid. Roscommon County Council was due almost €7.8 million from housing tenants last year - but less than €6.9 million was paid. The council says this is a collection rate of 89 per cent, in line with 2024. There was a higher collection rate, of 96 per cent, for housing loans. item.title: Fianna Fáil's support falls to lowest level since last general election
item.description: Fianna Fáil’s support has fallen to 15 percent, its lowest level since the last general election. The party is the biggest loser in the latest Red C poll for the Business Post. Fianna Fáil is down three points this month, while Fine Gael edges up to 18 percent, leaving the coalition on a combined record low of 33 percent. item.title: Local concern raised over fixed fare systems by taxi companies
item.description: Concern has been raised over fixed fare systems by taxi companies. Groups representing drivers want stricter regulations for taxi apps, and say those offering cheaper rates to passengers are undermining the future of the industry. The Oireachtas Transport Committee also heard how the number of taxi licences has fallen by a quarter since 2009, with a particular shortage of drivers in rural areas. item.title: Councillor calls for Longford to be included on fast track train line to Dublin
item.description: A Longford Councillor has called for a meeting with Irish Rail over plans for a fast track line from Mullingar to Dublin. Fine Gael's Peggy Nolan wants the fast track line to start from Longford and believes the town could be at a disadvantage if it's not implemented. The issue has also been raised at recent council meetings in Leitrim. Cllr Nolan says she doesn't want Longford to be left behind when it comes to public transport: Advertisement
